title: Custom code and snippets
when_to_use: Adding analytics, pixels, chat widgets, site-wide CSS/JS, or anything the user phrases as put in header/footer/functions.php.
principles: Outcome over file path: “put in header” usually means print in <head> (wp_head), not edit header.php.
Never edit the active theme’s header.php / footer.php / functions.php — theme updates wipe it; block themes often have no usable header.php; edits are hard to undo.
Ahentic Code Snippets (site / head / footer / wp_head injection for HTML, CSS, JS, or PHP) are Premium — if the ability is missing, say so (missing_ability) and soft-gate; do not invent file edits.
Custom HTML blocks (core/html) with HTML inside a specific page/post are Free editor work — not the same as Code Snippets. Use that only when the user wants page-scoped markup, not site chrome.
Before adding analytics/tracking, list plugins — warn if Site Kit, MonsterInsights, ExactMetrics, GA Google Analytics, or similar already injects tags.
Do not default to installing Site Kit when the user pasted a measurement ID or script and wants that snippet on the site.
Do not fake site-wide tracking or header scripts as a Custom HTML block on one page unless the user clearly wants page-only.
steps: Clarify whether they want site-wide / head / footer injection, page-scoped HTML, or a full analytics plugin setup with Google account flow.
Call ahentic/list-plugins to detect existing analytics/tag managers.
If a Premium snippet ability exists: upsert with location head/body_open/footer, HITL preview of exact code, avoid duplicate tags.

If no snippet ability (free / not installed): set missing_ability (e.g. ahentic/upsert-code-snippet), explain Code Snippets are Premium, and offer: Custom HTML block for page-only HTML, Customizer Additional CSS for CSS-only, paste via a trusted snippets plugin they already have, or upgrade.
For PHP/login-rename/server redirects: explain that needs Premium PHP snippets with probe/arm — do not write PHP into the Ahentic plugin.
anti_patterns: Installing Site Kit every time someone says “add GA”.
Stacking a second analytics injector when one is already active.
Dumping arbitrary PHP into Ahentic’s plugin files.
Pretending a Custom HTML block on one page is the same as site-wide head/footer injection.
